q: Agent configuration is an inspectable part of the software supply chain.
r: IC1: static supply-chain scan of MCP, permission and skill declarations; no effect on cost or quality of coding agents, so not clearly SDD, context mechanism or agent evaluation.

q: we track 143 SKILL.md files through 631 commit-file history records
r: Include: mining study of maintenance of agent skill files (context mechanism) with a bounded transfer-task test on coding agents.

q: Following repository-specific norms requires identifying guidance dispersed across repository sources
r: Include: acquires repository norms as guidance packages for existing coding agents and evaluates compliance, functional success and token cost on 121 tasks, three models.

q: Existing scanners catch at most 46% of loosening directives
r: IC1: large-scale content and security study of agent skills in general (1.53 million), not coding-agent development or its cost and quality.

q: This paper is an experience report and an operating model, not an empirical validation
r: EC3: single-author experience report and opinion-style operating model with no empirical evaluation.

q: The tasks are 60 ManyIFEval writing tasks
r: IC1: theoretical model of instruction-file curation tested on writing instruction-following tasks, not coding agents on software tasks.

q: We focus on scientific tasks whose outputs are executable Python programs evaluated in a sandbox.
r: IC1: experience-representation study for LLM agents on scientific problem tasks, not coding agents on software development.

q: Repository-scale coding depends on an edit-time working set of coupled facts.
r: Include: controlled interventions across seven model families and two harnesses on repository-scale coding tasks, including convention-file effects.
